title: Nebraska's 1st Congressional District election, 2026
description: The general election for Nebraska's 1st Congressional District will be held on November 3, 2026. Incumbent Republican Mike Flood, first elected in a 2022 special election and re-elected in 2024 with 60.1% of the vote, is seeking a third full term. He will face Democratic nominee Chris Backemeyer, a former U.S. deputy assistant secretary of state who defeated Eric Moyer in the May 12 Democratic primary. Libertarian nominee Nik Sandman is also on the ballot. Independent candidate Austin Ahlman, an investigative journalist, announced his candidacy in May 2026 and is working to secure ballot access by collecting 2,000 valid signatures. The district, which includes Lincoln, Norfolk, and much of eastern Nebraska, is considered safely Republican by nonpartisan analysts.
polling_note: Polls are limited to two surveys conducted by Democratic-leaning firms. Both show incumbent Mike Flood leading Democratic nominee Chris Backemeyer, with independent Austin Ahlman drawing single-digit support in one poll. The Cook Political Report, Inside Elections, and Sabato's Crystal Ball all rate the race as 'Safe Republican.'

candidates.name: Mike Flood
candidates.summary: Mike Flood is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Nebraska's 1st Congressional District, first elected in a 2022 special election and re-elected in 2024. He previously served in the Nebraska Legislature from 2005 to 2013, including six years as the youngest Speaker of the Legislature in state history. Flood founded Flood Communications, a statewide media network of radio and television stations, and earned his law degree from the University of Nebraska.

candidates.name: Chris Backemeyer
candidates.summary: Chris Backemeyer is the Democratic nominee for Nebraska's 1st Congressional District. A former deputy assistant secretary of state for Iranian Affairs and for Assistance Coordination in the Bureau of Near Eastern Affairs, he served 20 years at the U.S. Department of State under both Democratic and Republican administrations, also serving on the White House National Security Council and as an advisor to Vice President Kamala Harris. He is a fifth-generation Nebraskan from Lincoln who earned a master's degree in international relations.

candidates.name: Austin Ahlman
candidates.summary: Austin Ahlman is an independent candidate for Nebraska's 1st Congressional District. A 28-year-old investigative journalist who previously worked for The Intercept and The American Prospect, Ahlman grew up in Norfolk and attended Macalester College. He announced his candidacy in May 2026 and is working to secure ballot access by collecting 2,000 valid signatures from district voters by the August 3, 2026 deadline. His campaign focuses on anti-corporate monopoly policies, affordability, and cutting ties with establishment politics.

candidates.name: Nik Sandman
candidates.summary: Nik Sandman is the Libertarian Party nominee for Nebraska's 1st Congressional District. A 77-year-old retired farmer and rural mail carrier from Lincoln, Sandman earned a bachelor's degree in philosophy from the University of Nebraska-Lincoln. He ran unopposed in the May 12 Libertarian primary and advocates for constitutional governance, fiscal conservatism, and congressional authority over war declarations.

forecast.rationale: Incumbent Republican Mike Flood is heavily favored in Nebraska's 1st District, which nonpartisan analysts (Cook, Inside Elections, Sabato's Crystal Ball) uniformly rate as Safe Republican. Flood won re-election in 2024 with 60.1% of the vote and the district's partisan baseline is strongly Republican. Available polling is limited to two Democratic-leaning firms (Tavern Research and Zenith Research), which modestly reduces confidence, but all three survey matchups show Flood leading Democrat Chris Backemeyer. Ahlman (I) remains a wild card as he works to secure ballot access, and Sandman (L) is a minor factor. District fundamentals and incumbency strongly favor a Republican hold.
